title: Claims service, lifecycle, PII, timers and checks
story: As an adjuster and compliance officer I can rely on a claim record with a governed lifecycle, encrypted PII, full audit, notes, tasks and regulatory timers that warn and breach on time.
acceptance: createClaim/getClaim/listClaims/transition/addNote/addTask/etc. exported per modules.md#claims; claims is sole writer of Claim.status; invalid transitions rejected with a typed error; tests/unit/claims/lifecycle.test.js covers every allowed and a sample of disallowed transitions
Fields marked x-pii in Claim.schema.json are encrypted at rest via ctx.crypto and decrypted on read for authorised roles; test asserts raw stored rows contain no plaintext PII and events contain none
Every mutation writes an audit entry and publishes the matching claim.* event in the same unit of work (outbox); tests/unit/claims/audit-events.test.js

On claim.reported timers are created from tenant timer definitions selected by loss state + LOB; sweepTimers(now) exported, publishes claim.timer.due and claim.timer.breached once each (idempotent) using ctx.clock; subscribe() runs it every 30s with setInterval().unref(); tests/unit/claims/timers.test.js uses a fake clock
claim.checks records coverage, evidence and triage results from their events (claim.coverage.verified etc. per the event list); tests/unit/claims/checks.test.js
Routes match openapi /claims paths with x-roles; tests/unit/claims/routes.test.js
brief: Implement service(ctx) in src/modules/claims/{index,service,lifecycle,pii,timers,routes}.js. Read architecture/overview.md section 7 for the exact states and transitions and encode them as a table in lifecycle.js. Use architecture/core-runtime-api.md for ctx.db, ctx.events, ctx.audit, ctx.crypto, ctx.clock, ctx.tenants and the tenant-bound ctx addendum; do not invent method names. Decision recorded by architecture: coverage/evidence results go in claim.checks, not sub-states; routing is owned by rules (it sets queue/assignee via a service function in modules.md#claims, not by writing status). PII: walk Claim.schema.json for x-pii, encrypt those paths on write, decrypt on read; never put PII in events or audit diffs (store field names only). Timers: timer definitions come from tenant config (see tenants/ examples being authored in parallel in S1-WFL-01; in tests use an inline fake tenant config with WI/IL style definitions). Timer lifecycle: pending -> due (warn threshold) -> breached, completing on the satisfying event or transition. sweepTimers(now) must be idempotent and handle a clock jump. Fake the policy, coverage and rules modules in tests/unit/claims/fakes.js. Run only node --test --disable-warning=ExperimentalWarning tests/unit/claims/.

verdicts.reason: All criteria met: 25/25 claims tests pass, lifecycle/PII/timers/checks/routes verified against contracts and openapi x-roles; module boots, sweepTimers exported

escapedDefects.summary: Claimants can see fraud score and SIU flags
No instant acknowledgment (REQ-12): acknowledge timer never met, KPI acknowledgment time null
